name: HexaEdit CE
summary: A hex editor that runs on the calculator itself.
description:
An on-calculator hex editor. It opens any TI-OS variable — programs, appvars, equations — as well as RAM and the ports, and it will show you the ROM without letting you write to it.

The main menu lists everything on the calculator in three columns, with size, VAT location and memory location beside each, and the free RAM and archive along the bottom. Beside those is EDB, the edit buffer size: a variable larger than that cannot be opened, and archiving or deleting something else is what makes room.

The editor does direct letter and digit entry — pressing A writes its ASCII code — along with cut, copy and paste, a find for short strings, a goto, an undo, and automatic little-endian decimal translation of up to three bytes. [clear] backs out of anything.

install.text: HexaEdit writes directly to RAM, to the ports and to any variable on the calculator, and it does not stop you making a mistake. A wrong write can crash the calculator, and in the worst case damage it permanently. Its author says plainly: make sure you know what you are doing before using it.
